messages:
maria: Quick sync — product asked for a single "effective cost" metric for each call that includes cache savings + routing deltas. two questions: do we show that at the per-call row in the console, or keep that as a hover-summary with the default = token-level breakdown? :thinking:
jon: I lean hover-summary. per-call number is useful but hides attribution. token breakdown helps debugging + chargebacks. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
alisha: Hover loses discoverability though. PMs will complain if they can’t see immediate cost impact of a rollout. maybe show both but lightweight for default? :eyes:
sam: Also we need to decide which cache savings to include. currently our prefetched-KV credits get applied at batch level in the router. If we roll them into per-call effective cost we need a deterministic split. otherwise numbers jump between samples.
evan: Agree with sam. proposal: compute effective_cost = raw_token_cost - apportioned_cache_credit + routing_delta. Apportion cache by token-length share of requests in a session window (30m). simple and deterministic.
maria: That apportionment idea sounds ok but we need to show methodology somewhere. Suggest a small link -> "how we compute effective cost" modal. also UX: default row shows "effective cost" but clicking expands token breakdown and cache line-item.
jon: Implementation note: telemetry event should include both representations so console and billing reconcile. i propose API change: /v1/usage?granularity=call returns both fields. sample payload:```json
{"costs": {"effective_cost": 0.0123, "token_cost": 0.015, "cache_credit": 0.0027, "routing_delta": -0.0004}}
```
alisha: love that. keep field names stable (snake_case vs camelCase debate again). i'd prefer snake_case for our backend logs, but console sdk expects camelCase. we should publish both or normalize in the frontend.
sam: small ops concern: if we compute apportionment with a 30m sliding window we must surface sampling/latency impact — apportioner job is O(n) per session bucket. need to cap with reservoir sampling if high qps. tagging this for eng-infra.
evan: I'll sketch the apportioner algorithm tomorrow. will include reservoir sampling fallback and how credits are zeroed for cold-starts.
metric-bot: new metric created: econ.effective_cost.apportioned — alerts: >3% diff vs token_cost for 5m window.
maria: Decisions: 1) expose effective_cost by default in row, with expandable token + cache line items. 2) API returns both fields (effective + token + cache + routing). 3) doc modal with math + sampling caveats. action items: @evan to draft apportioner algorithm, @sam to check scaling ops, @alisha to mock console affordance, @jon to add API schema PR. :thumbsup:
jon: filing API PR in a bit. will tag for review.
alisha: will do a quick Figma tonight and drop screenshots in #eng-platform-design.
sam: will run a load check on apportioner pattern next week.
maria: thanks all — will circle back after PR + mock. :rocket:
